headline: Claude Fable 5 is now available globally as US lifts export restrictions
summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 AI model is being restored and made globally available starting July 1, following the lifting of US export control restrictions.
details: Anthropic has confirmed it will begin restoring access to Claude Fable 5 this Wednesday, July 1. This follows the lifting of US export control restrictions that previously limited its availability.

The AI model's temporary restriction was reportedly due to the need for additional safety testing, a measure that garnered attention from figures like Donald Trump. With these concerns addressed, the model is now cleared for a global release.

Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 AI model is back! Global access begins July 1 after US export restrictions were lifted.

headline_marked: [[Senior SWE-Bench]] evaluates AI agents as senior engineers on complex tasks
headline: Senior SWE-Bench evaluates AI agents as senior engineers on complex tasks
summary: A new open-source benchmark, Senior SWE-Bench, assesses AI agents on complex, real-world software engineering tasks. Even top frontier models fail to meet senior-level correctness over 75% of the time.
details: Senior SWE-Bench is a new open-source benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on software engineering tasks at a senior engineer level. It moves beyond junior-level assessments, focusing on realistic instructions and complex problem-solving.

The benchmark features tasks with natural language instructions, mirroring real-world communication. It includes a validation agent that uses expert-designed recipes to create adaptive behavioral tests for submitted solutions.

Bug tasks in Senior SWE-Bench reflect tricky user reports, requiring significant investigation, debugging, and starting services. These are sourced from pull requests that demanded extensive runtime investigation, including logs and profiling data.

The evaluation scores "tasteful solves" by combining runtime correctness with several quality metrics based on observed codebase practices. Verifiers and validation can also test against unstated, load-bearing codebase practices.

Current top-performing frontier models struggle significantly, failing to complete tasks with senior-level correctness and taste over 75% of the time. This highlights the substantial gap between current AI capabilities and senior human engineers.

Tasks are sourced from PRs in diverse repositories, spanning libraries to multi-service applications, authored by experienced engineers. They focus on multi-phase, multi-stack feature PRs and complex bug/performance issues.

Senior SWE-Bench tasks are long-horizon, often requiring hundreds of steps for even the strongest agents. They also reflect natural communication, with a median instruction length 31% that of SWE-Bench Pro, and can span multiple services, touching an average of 11 files per feature task.
